{"children": [
{"start":"spya-mb2psk","title":"Classification Topics Overview","gist":"Darwin lists the classification questions—natural system, affinities, morphology, embryology, rudimentary organs—he will address.","sourceHeading":"CLASSIFICATION, groups subordinate to groups...","needsDeeper":false,"why":"Single list, not several arguments."},
{"start":"spya-tu03uw","title":"Groups Within Groups","gist":"Divergence and extinction from dominant species naturally produce the nested groups-within-groups seen in classification.","sourceHeading":"","needsDeeper":false,"why":"One sustained argument using the diagram."},
{"start":"spya-ztm2qa","title":"The Natural System Debated","gist":"Darwin argues the Natural System reflects genealogical descent rather than an arbitrary scheme or a plan of creation.","sourceHeading":"","needsDeeper":false,"why":"Single continuous argument on meaning of natural system."},
{"start":"spya-ud02kz","title":"Value of Characters","gist":"Classificatory importance of a character depends on constancy and correlation, not on its physiological or adaptive importance.","sourceHeading":"","needsDeeper":false,"why":"One sustained argument across several examples."},
{"start":"spya-d40x4f","title":"Embryonic and Chained Affinities","gist":"Embryonic characters and chains of intermediate forms both reveal true descent-based affinity even without one shared definition.","sourceHeading":"","needsDeeper":false,"why":"Connected discussion of two related classificatory clues."},
{"start":"spya-qk0atb","title":"Rank and Genealogy","gist":"Geographic distribution aids classification, group ranks are largely arbitrary, and true classification must be strictly genealogical, as illustrated by languages.","sourceHeading":"","needsDeeper":false,"why":"One extended argument with a supporting analogy."},
{"start":"spya-zrem2e","title":"Descent in Varieties and Species","gist":"Just as varieties are classed by descent despite differences, species classification already tacitly relies on descent for sexes, larvae, and monsters.","sourceHeading":"","needsDeeper":false,"why":"Continuous argument building one claim about descent."},
{"start":"spya-j8sgvq","title":"Analogical versus Real Affinity","gist":"Descent explains why trifling but correlated characters mark true affinity while adaptive resemblances between distinct lines are misleading.","sourceHeading":"","needsDeeper":false,"why":"One sustained argument distinguishing affinity types."},
{"start":"spya-s6snj5","title":"Dominance, Extinction, Aberrance","gist":"Dominant groups spread and supplant others while extinction isolates aberrant forms, explaining complex radiating affinities and the section's summary.","sourceHeading":"","needsDeeper":false,"why":"Sequence of related claims culminating in one summary."},
{"start":"spya-mzbeg7","title":"Morphology","gist":"Shared structural plans across species, like the homologous bones of limbs, reveal unity of type beneath varied functions.","sourceHeading":"Morphology","needsDeeper":false,"why":"Single topic heading, one sustained point."}
]}
